messages.subject: [Rattle] RGtk2 v 2.20.14 with R v 2.13.1 issues under MS/Windows
messages.subject_clean: [Rattle] RGtk2 v 2.20.14 with R v 2.13.1 issues under MS/Windows
messages.body_plain:
The release of RGtk2 in June (version 2.20.14) for R 2.13.1 appears to have an issue on some installations of R.

The following error is reported for some users - but not all
(e.g., I am not able to replicate it on MS/Windows so far):

===================================================================
> rattle()
Error in inDL(x, as.logical(local), as.logical(now), ...) :
  unable to load shared object 'C:/..../2.13/RGtk2/libs/i386/RGtk2.dll':
  LoadLibrary failure:  The device is not ready.

Failed to load RGtk2 dynamic library, attempting to install it.
trying URL 'http://..../gtk+-bundle_2.22.1-20101229_win64.zip'
Content type 'application/zip' length 25830230 bytes (24.6 Mb)
opened URL
downloaded 24.6 Mb

Error : .onLoad failed in loadNamespace() for 'RGtk2', details:
  call: unzip(path, exdir = .windows_gtk_path)
  error: 'exdir' does not exist
Error in rattle() : could not find function "gtkBuilderNew"
===================================================================

Apparently version 2.20.8 works okay (with R 2.11) but I'm not sure it is available for this release of R.

Further discussion is available from http://groups.google.com/group/ggobi/browse_thread/thread/b177af290a04d81e.

It would be useful to hear of any others with this problem and particularly anyone who has successfully worked around the problem. It seems to all be okay on a clean installation of R and RGtk2 - but somehow old libraries are affecting it when R and RGtk2 have been previously installed (but not always).

Once a solution is found I will add it to the trouble shooting section of http://rattle.togaware.com/rattle-install-mswindows.html.

Regards,
Graham

messages.body_plain:
Thanks for the question Tony.

I guess it depends on how up-to-date you want to be.

For me I update to the latest version of R every 6 months (which is the R release cycle). I of course always update rattle on each release of rattle.

Then, once rattle is installed, I check regularly what package updates are available, and then install them - all done automatically through a rattle function. Do have a play with rattleInfo() - it will tell you the packages that Rattle uses and that can be upgraded.

messages.body_plain:
With the imminent release of the Rattle book (http://www.amazon.com/Data-Mining-Rattle-Excavating-Knowledge/dp/1441998896) there is some good news regarding the installation of Rattle on MS/Windows (or more precisely with the installation of RGtk2 on Windows).

With the release of RGtk2 2.20.17 overnight this hurdle appears to have been fixed. RGtk2 is now able to successfully install GTK+ on machines where it could not previously do so.

For all tested platforms (now including Mac OS X), the basic installation instructions are now:

Install R 2.13.1
Startup R
> install.packages("rattle")
> rattle()

This will just work if the GTK+ libraries are installed. On GNU/Linux, they generally are installed. On Mac OS X, you will be prompted to install them if they are not already installed. On Windows you'll see a message about a missing library and then be prompted to install them if they are not already installed.

Details are available from http://rattle.togaware.com.

Regards,
Graham
